title: Wrist Curl
summary: Seated dumbbell wrist curl, forearms on the thighs: forearm flexors 1.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: dumbbells or barbell (Olympic bar) or EZ curl bar.

muscles.why: The wrist flexors bend the wrist palm-up.

setup.text: Sit with forearms on the thighs, wrists past the knees.

form_cues.cue: Let the bar roll to your fingers
form_cues.why: Letting the wrist extend fully at the bottom.
Curling up with the wrist only.

form_cues.cue: Keep forearms flat on the support
Let the dumbbell roll to the fingers at the bottom

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.text: Lifting the forearms to move the weight.
mistakes.fix: Use a light load with full range.

misconceptions.reality: Light and heavy loads gave similar growth when sets were taken close to failure. Heavy loads build more strength.

lower_risk.text: The app adds no ramp-up sets here. If the muscle is not warm from earlier work, make the first set a little lighter.

Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 10% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 2 reps in reserve in the 10-15 rep range. Low-risk to push close to failure.
Pick a variation, range and setup you can train pain-free.

notes: Forearm exercises have not been compared for growth in a study the app cites.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
